Risk: Heat treatment of gears and shafts is the most energy intensive stage in driveline, axle, and transmission manufacturing due to continuous high temperature operations and repeated thermal cycles. Energy costs therefore constitute a significant portion of Carraro India Limited operating expenditure. The Company remains largely dependent on non renewable fuels such as PNG and diesel, exposing it to energy price volatility, carbon related regulations, and rising customer and investor expectations on emissions reduction and energy efficiency. Opportunity: Effective energy management reduces the energy and carbon footprint of products. As supplier emissions face increasing regulatory and customer scrutiny, improved energy efficiency enhances competitiveness, supports preferential contracting, and strengthens cost positioning.

Carraro India Limited is increasing the share of renewable energy, including solar and wind, to reduce dependence on fossil fuels and lower greenhouse gas emissions. During 2025-26, the Company consumed 40.67 Lakh kWh of renewable electricity across Plant 1 and Plant 2 through onsite captive solar. Additionally, Carraro India Limited is progressing towards phasing out propane through planned fuel switch initiatives. These measures are expected to mitigate long term energy cost volatility, regulatory exposure, and deliver operational efficiencies alongside reputational benefits.

Risk: Global and domestic regulatory developments including India’s Net Zero 2070 commitment, the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, and the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) are increasing climate related compliance requirements for automotive OEMs and component manufacturers. Physical climate risks also pose challenges to manufacturing continuity and resilience. Opportunity: Strong climate governance improves risk management and positions the Company to benefit from a lower carbon footprint, preferential contracting, and sustained market access through enhanced stakeholder trust.

Carraro India Limited monitors Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions and is strengthening its climate management framework. The Company has initiated its transition through investments in renewable and cleaner energy sources, reducing regulatory, market, and energy price risks. Ongoing efforts focus on improving emissions data quality, visibility, and organisational preparedness for evolving climate related regulatory requirements.

Risk: While most waste generated is non hazardous, improper handling or disposal of hazardous and industrial waste could lead to regulatory non compliance, environmental damage, operational disruption, and reputational impact, particularly amid tightening regulations and heightened OEM supply chain scrutiny. Opportunity: Increased focus on material efficiency, circularity, and compliance requirements such as Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) presents opportunities to strengthen waste reduction, recycling, and recovery practices. These initiatives enhance reputational value, stakeholder confidence, and can deliver cost savings through reduced disposal and improved material recovery.

Carraro India Limited ensures regulatory compliance through waste segregation at source, authorised handling and disposal, and continuous monitoring of waste recovery. These processes are reinforced through third party audits and partnerships with authorised recyclers. To reduce single use plastic, the Company has implemented returnable supplier packaging and reuse of polypropylene sheets, supporting both compliance and material efficiency. In the reporting period, 94% of waste was recycled through authorised waste vendors.

Carraro India Limited relies on third party freshwater sources for domestic and industrial use. Maharashtra is classified as a water stressed state, with declining groundwater availability reported by the Central Ground Water Board, including in Pune district where Carraro India Limited. operates. Increased scrutiny by pollution control authorities also heightens compliance and operational risks.

Carraro India Limited has installed advanced effluent treatment systems, implemented closed loop recycling with zero liquid discharge, and adopted real time water quality monitoring. These measures, supported by regulatory compliance and employee training, reduce freshwater dependence. The Company is also exploring groundwater recharge initiatives to strengthen long term water stewardship.

Human capital represents a material opportunity due to the skill intensive and precision driven nature of automotive component manufacturing. A skilled, engaged, and stable workforce supports product quality and operational excellence. Focused workforce planning, skill development, safety management, and employee engagement improve productivity, reduce defects and attrition, and enable new product development. Strong human capital practices also enhance supplier credibility, support long term OEM relationships, and improve organisational resilience amid technological and industry shifts.

Manufacturing operations involving machining, forging, cutting, and heat treatment present inherent occupational health and safety risks. Inadequate risk identification or control may result in accidents, injuries, downtime, and regulatory non compliance. Lapses in safety performance can also increase insurance costs, damage reputation, reduce morale, and increase attrition, adversely affecting productivity and business continuity.

Carraro India Limited has established structured health and safety management systems, including defined safety procedures, machine safeguarding, regular risk assessments, and preventive maintenance. Employees receive periodic safety training, induction programmes, and awareness sessions. Compliance is reinforced through inspections, incident monitoring, and corrective actions. Periodic audits and reviews support continuous improvement, reduce incidents, and strengthen a culture of safety.

Risk: Following the Company’s listing, corporate governance and business ethics have become increasingly material due to enhanced regulatory scrutiny and disclosure requirements. Gaps in governance processes or ethical conduct could expose the Company to regulatory, legal, financial, and reputational risks. Opportunity: Strong governance enhances transparency, accountability, and risk management, supporting investor confidence, access to capital, and long term value creation. Governance maturity also strengthens trust with OEM customers and business partners, positively influencing supplier relationships, ratings, and cost of capital.

Carraro India Limited operates under a structured governance framework supported by an experienced Board, defined policies, internal controls, and regulatory compliance systems. Governance practices are periodically reviewed and strengthened to align with evolving requirements and reinforce ethical conduct across the organisation.

Evaluation of Provisions, disclosures and analysis with respect to direct tax litigations The Company has various disputes/litigations related to direct taxes at various levels of appellate authorities. The evaluation of the Company’s position and determination of possible outcome of these disputes and provisions and related disclosures, if any, required to be made in the books involves significant management judgment. Considering the materiality of the amounts and degree of judgement and estimation involved to determine financial impact and the possible outcome of such disputes/litigations, we have considered this matter as a key audit matter. Refer Note 3(f) and note 33 to the standalone financial statements.

Principal Audit Procedures Performed: • We assessed management’s processes and tested the internal controls implemented for the identification, recognition and measurement of tax positions and its assessment of the potential impact on the Company. • We received a statement of all ongoing disputes/litigations along with the necessary documentation and - We evaluated management’s assessments including advice/opinion obtained from external consultants/ legal advisors with respect to prospects of success of appeals and tax proceedings. - We involved our internal experts to challenge the management’s position on the select litigations and to consider legal precedence and other rulings in evaluating management’s position on these tax positions. - We also assessed the adequacy and appropriateness of the disclosures made by the management in the notes to the standalone financial statements.
